# Extraction, structural fidelity and citation audit

**Reviewed:** 2026-10-23.  
**Documentation baseline:** [`d9d48bb`](https://github.com/UnknownAlienHuman/eliot-research/tree/d9d48bbbf115a7a8d4d18c1b41ac617ebc7f345e).  
**Legacy code baseline:** [`main@7c034569`](https://github.com/UnknownAlienHuman/eliot-research/tree/7c034569b908d3b03a8b821b7c537477a24b10f7).

This continuation checks the path from an uploaded file to canonical readable text, structural blocks and exact
references. It compares the target design with current Cloudflare conversion/search behavior, the old Eliot conversion
adapter and structural projector, and the selected Docling mechanism. Findings are design gaps or boundaries, not
claims that the replacement runtime already exists.

## Findings and required corrections

| # | Gap at the baseline | Required correction |
|---|---|---|
| 32 | **“Supported files use `toMarkdown`” treated provider support as a static fact.** Cloudflare exposes `env.AI.toMarkdown().supported()`, while extensions, MIME values and conversion behavior can change independently of Eliot. The old adapter also rejects any additive provider response field through exact-key matching, making a harmless API extension a conversion failure. | Keep deterministic local UTF-8 Markdown/text/CSV paths. At setup or owner-requested diagnostics, read and cache the current supported format list with a checked time; do not call it before every upload. Admission checks name, observed MIME and current support without pretending extension is authority. Decode required `ConversionResult` fields and discriminants while ignoring unknown additive fields. Pin installed types at implementation time; do not recreate a strict provider-contract bureaucracy. |
| 33 | **Direct Workers AI Markdown Conversion and AI Search OCR were conflated.** Current direct `toMarkdown` documentation describes PDF structure/text extraction but exposes no OCR switch. OCR for scanned PDFs is an AI Search indexing option. An AI Search OCR chunk is not automatically Eliot's retained canonical representation or an exact original-page citation. | The baseline converter may publish a usable head only from retained ordered text. If direct conversion of a scan is empty or unusable, retain the original as `stored_needs_conversion`. Do not enable hidden AI Search OCR and then cite its unretained output as canonical evidence. A later OCR route is one explicit converter path only when it returns a retained complete text artifact plus page/region mapping and declared generation; otherwise accept owner/agent-supplied normalized Markdown as a new revision. No default Python/Docling service or second document platform is added. |
| 34 | **Page and table coordinates were not separated from exact canonical byte identity.** `toMarkdown` parses PDF pages sequentially and uses `StructTree` when available; without it, text is returned as-is. Page headings in output are useful but do not prove perfect layout, reading order or table reconstruction. | Store converter ID/version/options, result ID, output format/digest/size and a small quality report with the source revision. Exact references always address UTF-8 bytes of the immutable stored readable representation. Original page/table/figure anchors are separate typed navigation hints with `verified`, `observed` or `unavailable` fidelity; never synthesize an exact page from a heading guess. Re-conversion or corrected mapping creates a new revision. |
| 35 | **Generated image descriptions could be mistaken for OCR or literal source text.** Cloudflare's image path resizes images, detects objects and asks a vision model for a description; animated GIF conversion uses only the first frame. This can aid discovery but cannot substantiate an exact quotation, number or label present in the image. | Mark model-produced image/figure descriptions as `generated_image_description`, retain model/converter provenance and keep them outside the primary quotation set. They may locate a figure or support an explicitly labelled visual summary, but quantitative/literal claims require retained OCR or human-provided text with mapping. Coverage names unprocessed frames, figures and image text instead of calling the source fully read. |
| 36 | **The old structural projector is useful but not sufficient as the target parser.** It provides bounded UTF-8 offsets, heading/fence awareness and deterministic identities, but its historical 32–64 KiB targets and oversized-line splitting can cut semantic structures. It does not by itself prove table, equation, figure or page semantics. | Reuse only the tested UTF-8 range, heading/fence and deterministic-key ideas. The target parser operates on the retained Markdown and emits typed blocks conservatively: a table only when a complete valid table is observed; code fences remain intact; headings/captions/definitions use exact context ranges; unknown layout remains prose. Split tables by valid row/column groups and repeat exact headers, following the selected Docling mechanism, rather than cutting rows or inventing structure. No model call is used for structural parsing. |
| 37 | **“Readable representation is valid” lacked a minimal acceptance rule.** The old code has many dispatch/receipt states but still cannot establish extraction fidelity. Conversely, one binary success flag would publish empty, truncated or obviously corrupt output. | Use three owner-visible states: `readable`, `readable_with_warnings`, `stored_needs_conversion`. Require a successful conversion result, nonempty valid UTF-8, bounded retained output and no explicit provider truncation/error before publishing a usable head. Cheap deterministic warnings may report suspiciously low text density, missing expected page output, unsupported objects or generated descriptions; they do not reject a language or claim semantic correctness. Store warnings and omissions, not a proof packet. |
| 38 | **The quality gate named Cyrillic/scans/tables but had no fixed corpus or pass criteria.** Without repeatable material, agents can declare extraction “tested” after one easy PDF. | Maintain a small representative fixture set only when implementation begins: native English and Russian PDFs, a scanned PDF, two-column paper, long table, footnotes, equation/code, office document, static HTML, rendered page and image/GIF. For each, record retained bytes, conversion state, section/table/page hints, exact non-ASCII range reopening and known omissions. The gate measures fidelity and failure honesty; it does not require every format to pass before unrelated product work continues. |

## Evidence checked

### Cloudflare primary documentation

- [Workers AI Markdown Conversion binding](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/features/markdown-conversion/usage/binding/) defines `ConversionResult`, `transform()` and the current `supported()` format-discovery method.
- [How Markdown Conversion works](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/features/markdown-conversion/how-it-works/) states that PDFs are parsed page-by-page, use `StructTree` when available and otherwise return page text as-is. It also describes generated image descriptions and first-frame-only GIF handling.
- [Conversion options](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers-ai/features/markdown-conversion/conversion-options/) currently expose output, image-language, HTML and PDF-metadata options, but not direct PDF OCR.
- [AI Search data sources](https://developers.cloudflare.com/ai-search/configuration/data-source/) expose OCR through `indexing_options.use_ocr`; this is a search-ingestion feature with separate limits and billing, not proof of a retained canonical Eliot representation.
- [AI Search indexing errors](https://developers.cloudflare.com/ai-search/troubleshooting/indexing-error-codes/) distinguish invalid PDF, conversion failure, empty conversion and oversized generated Markdown.

### Eliot and donor code

- [`packages/cloudflare-markdown/src/markdown-conversion.ts`](https://github.com/UnknownAlienHuman/eliot-research/blob/7c034569b908d3b03a8b821b7c537477a24b10f7/packages/cloudflare-markdown/src/markdown-conversion.ts) contains a useful deterministic local-text path, but also an exact provider-object shape check and a large context/dispatch/failure contract that should not be copied into the replacement.
- [`packages/retrieval/src/structural-projector.ts`](https://github.com/UnknownAlienHuman/eliot-research/blob/7c034569b908d3b03a8b821b7c537477a24b10f7/packages/retrieval/src/structural-projector.ts) provides reusable UTF-8 offsets, heading/fence handling and deterministic item identity; its old item sizing and generic oversized-line split are not the target table/layout semantics.
- [The previous source-lifecycle design](https://github.com/UnknownAlienHuman/eliot-research/blob/7c034569b908d3b03a8b821b7c537477a24b10f7/docs/implementation/source-lifecycle.md) already requires immutable originals/readable representations and exact revision ranges while rejecting the old proof/generation envelope.
- [Docling HybridChunker at the selected pin](https://github.com/docling-project/docling-core/blob/b359e1c377aa8e3846ffb4100f7b513eb89ebd0c/docling_core/transforms/chunker/hybrid_chunker.py) repeats table headers, preserves document metadata/context and splits oversized tables into valid row/column groups. Eliot copies this mechanism, not the Python runtime.

## Owning-document changes to apply

- **Architecture:** distinguish exact readable-representation bytes from best-effort original-file navigation and explicitly refuse hidden OCR-as-evidence.
- **Implementation §§4–7:** add conversion profile/fidelity facts, supported-format discovery, simple acceptance states, explicit OCR boundary, conservative typed anchors and additive-tolerant provider parsing.
- **Map stages 1–3:** make scanned/empty conversion, two-column/table/page fidelity and generated-image handling completion checks.
- **Donors:** record the direct-conversion/OCR boundary and the exact subset retained from the legacy adapter/projector and Docling.

## Verification boundary

No live `toMarkdown` or AI Search OCR call, production file, installed package, application build, benchmark or migration
was run. Current documentation supports the boundary above; actual conversion quality and response/type details must be
checked against pinned installed packages and the representative corpus during the Library/Search vertical slices.
